title: Lunar orbiter among upcoming NASA CLPS task orders
summary: NASA is set to award three additional lunar missions this year through its Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program, including a new orbiter to replace the aging Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

title: U.S. Space Force adds second surveillance sensor to Japanese constellation
summary: The U.S. Space Force launched QZS-7, adding a second surveillance sensor to Japan's navigation satellite constellation. This completes a bilateral program to host U.S. sensors aboard Japanese satellites.

title: Wallops gears up for an increase in launches
summary: Wallops Island is preparing for a significant increase in launches, prompting calls for infrastructure upgrades to support companies and workers. This surge highlights the need for timely improvements to accommodate growing space industry demands.

title: Spire and PlanetiQ win NOAA radio-occultation contracts
summary: NOAA awarded contracts to Spire Global and PlanetiQ for radio occultation data to support terrestrial and space weather forecasts. The contracts aim to enhance weather prediction capabilities.

title: Cheaper launch has moved the spacecraft bottleneck. Mass is out, surface area is in.
summary: The reduction in launch costs has shifted the primary constraint in spacecraft design from mass to surface area. This change reflects how advancements in launch technology have altered the challenges faced in space missions.

title: Blue Origin outlines plans for second Cape Canaveral launch pad
summary: Blue Origin announced plans to expand its Florida launch site by adding a second pad for a larger version of its New Glenn rocket. This move aims to enhance the company's launch capabilities at Cape Canaveral.

title: Intuitive Machines wins contract for three GEO satellites

title: Bulgaria advances project to launch new space, defense innovation hub
summary: Bulgaria's government has approved a draft memorandum with EnduroSat to develop a new space and defense innovation hub. The collaboration aims to advance the country's space and defense sectors.

title: In-Orbit Services Market to Generate $3 Billion in Revenue Over the Next Decade
summary: Novaspace's report projects that in-orbit services will generate $3 billion in revenue over the next decade. This highlights the early development and growing potential of emerging space services.

title: CesiumAstro buys semiconductor specialist to boost constellation plans
summary: CesiumAstro has acquired semiconductor specialist Jariet Technologies to enhance its in-house capabilities for its future communications constellation. The move aims to strengthen CesiumAstro's phased-array antenna technology for satellite communications.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 15, 1977: Mysterious 'Wow!' Signal boosts search for E.T.
summary: On Aug. 15, 1977, astronomers detected the unexplained 'Wow!' signal using Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope, which remains a mystery in the search for extraterrestrial life.

summary: Experts warn that the growing moon race could lead to the lunar surface being used as a dumping ground for old rockets. They emphasize the need for regulations to prevent environmental damage on the moon.

summary: A volunteer developed a machine-learning tool to identify rare clouds as part of a NASA-supported project. The Space Cloud Watch initiative aims to study changes in cloud behavior, such as their increased frequency and lower altitude.

summary: NASA's COFFIES team developed an AI model to predict storm-causing active regions on the Sun, addressing the growing need to forecast space weather for future space exploration. The technology aims to enhance understanding of solar dynamics and mitigate risks to missions and infrastructure.

title: Total Solar Eclipse in Sunflower Field
summary: A total solar eclipse was observed across parts of Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, the Atlantic Ocean, Spain, and Portugal on August 12, 2026. A partial eclipse was also visible in parts of the U.S.
